name: Mid Michigan Wood Specialties
old_description: Custom BUILT DOORS AND DRAWERS that save you time, labor, and callbacks.
about:
Mid Michigan Wood Specialties was founded in 2006 in Lyons, Michigan. What began with three routers in a basement has grown into a manufacturing partner for cabinetmakers and builders across the United States.

The company specializes exclusively in cabinet components: cabinet doors, drawer fronts, dovetail drawer boxes, and face frames. Using precision woodworking and dovetail joinery, the shop produces parts built to customer specifications. Facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Its customers include cabinetmakers, builders, and contractors throughout Michigan and the broader U.S. market. The firm serves residential and commercial construction projects that require ready-to-install door and drawer components.

Founded by former cabinetmakers, the business was built to solve the labor and scheduling pressures they knew firsthand. The team emphasizes on-time delivery of components that arrive ready to install, allowing builders to focus on assembly rather than part fabrication. By limiting its scope to doors and drawers, the company aims to reduce callbacks and keep projects on schedule.

name: Midland Plastics, Inc.

about:
Midland Plastics, Inc. was founded in 1945 in New Berlin, Wisconsin, and has operated as a domestic manufacturer of plastic products for nearly eight decades. The company began as a plastics fabricator and has since expanded into a full-service distributor and custom manufacturer of high-performance plastics.

Today, Midland Plastics maintains a large inventory of plastic sheet, rod, and tube, and provides custom manufacturing services including CNC machining, thermoforming, vacuum forming, pressure forming, custom extrusions, and precision fabrication. The facility offers production cutting and forming capabilities for both prototype and production volumes, though specific headcount and facility size are not disclosed.

The company serves a range of industries including packaging, transportation (truck liners), medical devices, industrial equipment, construction (windows, skylights), signage and displays, and safety equipment (machine guards, containment panels). Customers include OEMs and fabricators requiring materials such as acrylic, polycarbonate, and polyethylene for applications ranging from display cases to medical components.

Midland Plastics emphasizes its long-standing U.S. manufacturing heritage, in-house material expertise, and the ability to guide customers to the optimal plastic for their specifications. The firm positions itself as a single source for both stock materials and custom-formed parts.

name: Midland West Manufacturing
old_description: Precision Machining & Fabrication Solutions Designed for Montana
about:
Midland West Manufacturing was founded in 1977 in Billings, Montana, by Stephen Pinnow and his father John Pinnow, starting with a single Miller Bobcat welder. The company moved through several smaller facilities before settling into its current 25,000-square-foot plant near the Lockwood Exit in 2006.

The shop combines fabrication, metal forming, machining, and design-build services under one roof. Its equipment lineup includes lathes, mills, press brakes, plate rolls, and fabricators, enabling structural, industrial, commercial, and custom fabrication; welding, handrailing, prototyping, and equipment repair; heavy-duty and CNC press brake work, plate and profile rolling, and straightening; traditional and CNC milling, metalizing, pipe threading, and line boring; plus SolidWorks CAD/CAM, shop drawings, design refinement, quoting, and material take-offs. The facility handles projects from one-off prototypes to high-production runs.

Midland West serves a diverse customer base across Montana and beyond, with noted work in agricultural equipment built for the state's plains and precision components for the aerospace sector. The company also supports industrial and commercial clients throughout Yellowstone County and the surrounding region.

The firm emphasizes its Montana heritage and community roots, positioning itself as more than a typical job shop. It cites quick turnaround times driven by in-house capabilities and industry connections, and claims the largest forming equipment in the region to take on jobs others cannot.

For two decades we manufactured our entire vest and tie collection for tuxedos. Today, our workforce of 100+ skilled sewers continue to manufacture products for an array of industries. We also specialize in custom cutting, sewing, and tailoring. Our capacity ranges from prototyping to small batch orders to 1000's of units per day. about:
Midwest Garment operates from La Crosse, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1948 as Desmond's Men's Wear and Desmond's Formal Wear. The business began as a regional distributor of tuxedos and, for two decades, manufactured its own vest and tie collections for the formalwear market. It continued in that role until 2003, when it shifted focus to broader textile manufacturing.

Today the company runs a commercial sewing, tailoring, and textile manufacturing operation staffed by more than 100 skilled sewers. Its capabilities span custom cutting, sewing, and tailoring, with specific processes that include single- and double-needle stitching, surge stitching, bar tacking, binding, blind hemming, sleeve setting, button covering and buttonholes, relabeling, heat-transfer labeling, fusing, strip cutting, and slitting. Production capacity ranges from prototyping and small batches to thousands of units per day.

Midwest Garment serves an array of industries requiring textile fabrication and repair, drawing on its heritage in formalwear to support customers needing custom sewn goods. While the company does not list specific sectors, its background in vest and tie production and its current service offering suggest work for apparel, uniform, and soft-goods markets.

The firm emphasizes its half-century of experience, a seasoned management team, and a diverse fleet of industrial sewing equipment as factors that enable on-time delivery of high-quality products.

name: Midwest Metal Fabrications
old_description: From concept to completion, we help OEMs, engineers, and manufacturers streamline production with expert
about:
Midwest Metal Fabrications has operated from Tallmadge, Ohio, for over 40 years. The company describes its origins as a hands-on partnership with customers, not merely a vendor relationship, a mindset that has driven steady growth. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides laser cutting up to 1-inch thick on a 5-by-10-foot table, press braking with 243 tons across a 14-foot opening, AWS-certified welding of stainless, aluminum, and carbon steel, CNC shearing on a 10-foot-wide shear, and CNC milling and turning from prototype through production. Metal finishing — powder coating, zinc plating, and galvanizing — is outsourced to qualified partners. Custom products include NEMA enclosures, weldments, steel bollards, and rack systems. The workforce averages 16 years of tenure; headcount and facility size are not published.

Customers span aerospace, automation, data centers, electrical contractors, food and beverage, housing, integrators, last-mile trucking, machine builders, manufacturing, nuclear, power, and transportation. Wind-energy components are also noted. The firm primarily serves Northeast Ohio — Akron, Cleveland, Canton, Columbus, Cincinnati, Toledo — but ships nationwide. Testimonials cite an Akron electrical contractor and Bevcorp in Eastlake as repeat clients.

The company emphasizes its collaborative approach and long-tenured team as differentiators. It holds ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100 certifications, and promotes competitive pricing, reliable turnaround, and a partner-oriented attitude — treating customers as partners rather than purchase orders. All work is performed in the USA.

name: Midwest Molding Inc
old_description: From concept and tooling to full-scale production, we deliver reliable, high-quality molded parts with advanced manufacturing capabilities and strict quality control.
about:
Midwest Molding operates from Plain City, Ohio, as a 100% employee-owned plastic injection molding company. The firm is ISO 9001 certified and emphasizes state-of-the-art manufacturing technologies to produce custom, high-quality, cost-competitive plastic parts and assemblies. No founding year or founders are disclosed in the available information.

The company provides custom injection molding for complex parts, including insert molding, multi-shot options, and gate cutting. Its capabilities span from early prototyping and mold design through full-scale mass production. Automation features include 6-axis robotic part removal, downstream automation, ultrasonic welding, and sub-assembly. The facility runs climate-controlled 24/7 with multiple all-electric injection molding machines, high-precision 5- and 6-axis servo robots, vision inspection systems, and cloud-based production monitoring. Tooling capacity reaches 40,000 lb, supporting hot runners, core pulls, and valve gates. Materials processed cover a wide variety of resins, including engineering-grade and high-temperature formulations.

Midwest Molding serves the automotive, medical, consumer products, and industrial sectors. The company positions itself as a partner from concept to full production, offering fast turnaround and flexible services backed by ISO-certified quality systems and skilled engineering and production teams.

The employee-ownership structure is highlighted as a differentiator, aligning workforce incentives with quality and customer outcomes. The company also cites advanced manufacturing technologies, high precision, and comprehensive support from design through delivery as key reasons customers choose them.

name: Midwest Plastics Inc.
about:
Midwest Plastics Inc., a family-owned manufacturer, was founded in 1945 and operates from a 48,000-square-foot facility in West St. Paul, Minnesota. The company has remained under family ownership since its inception, serving customers with custom and standard plastic products.

The company provides injection molding, thermoforming, and packaging services. Injection molding produces electronic housings, machine parts, gears, consumer products, medical components, hardware, and houseware items. Thermoforming capabilities cover machine covers, shrouds, blisters, clamshells, CRT bezels, printed-circuit-board storage trays, medical trays, automotive and aerospace components, and point-of-purchase displays. Packaging services include radio-frequency and heat sealing, boxing, labeling, collating, assembly, sorting, and shipping. The facility also supports prototype development for thermoformed parts.

Midwest Plastics serves the medical, automotive, aerospace, defense, energy, and telecommunications sectors. Its customer base includes the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, and manufacturers of medical devices, electronic equipment, and consumer goods. The company also produces a line of consumer organizers, kitchen utensil drawers, garbage bag dispensers, and cutting boards sold directly through its website.

The company emphasizes end-to-end service from concept through design, manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution. Engineers review product designs and advise on material selection, focusing on quality design and cost-effective tooling. Trained operators run efficient equipment, while in-house quality-control personnel conduct frequent inspections to ensure consistency. Packaging receives special attention to meet specific customer requirements.

name: Midwest Sheet Metal Co
old_description: Midwest Sheet Metal's Machine Shop is a complete, full service facility, specializing in custom tool and die, jigs and fixtures.  We are a  leading provider of innovative, practical, quality machining and fabrication.  No job is too big or too small.  Each job is given an unwavering level of attention to detail.  Over the years, Midwest Sheet Metal is proud to have earned a loyal customer base built on service, knowledge, trust, quality workmanship and competitive pricing.   We have trained, skilled and experienced personnel, with the right equipment, tools and knowledge to efficiently achieve your product goals.
about:
Midwest Sheet Metal Company operates from Springfield, Missouri, in the heart of the Ozark Mountain region. The business is a second-generation, family-owned operation; Jan Davis’s father, Dave, began his career there in 1957 and owned the company for more than 25 years. Today, Chris and Jan Davis have led the firm for over 15 years, continuing a legacy of custom fabrication and machining that the company describes as spanning more than 50 years.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication and precision machining services. Its capabilities include custom fabrication, a full-service machine shop, precision tool and die work, prototype design and fabrication, shearing, cutting, bending, forming, punching, sawing, rolling, and welding. The facility maintains a large in-stock inventory of aluminum (including Tread Brite and colored grades), stainless steel, carbon steel, and structural shapes, and the company notes it is the area’s largest supplier of Aluminum Tread Brite. A deep bench of personnel—many with 10 to 20-plus years of tenure—supports the operation, which also houses a machine shop specializing in jigs, fixtures, special tooling, and die repair.

Midwest Sheet Metal serves customers across a variety of industries, with product lines that include racing components and custom semi-truck sunvisors. The machine shop’s expertise in automotive stampings, fuel-injection parts, and small electric motor components further reflects a client base in automotive racing, heavy trucking, and general industrial manufacturing.

The company emphasizes its combination of scale and personal attention: a broad inventory and full-service capacity paired with one-to-one customer service. Its differentiators include a multi-decade workforce, extensive press-brake tooling, and a reputation for craftsmanship delivered at competitive prices.

name: Midwest Solar Power
old_description: Midwest Solar Power LLC was founded in 2009 and brought together their backgrounds in construction, project management, and customer service to modernize the solar installation business.
about:
Founded in 2009 in Madison, Wisconsin, Midwest Solar Power LLC was started by professionals with backgrounds in construction, project management, and customer service who aimed to modernize the solar installation business.

The company provides turnkey solar installation services for residential and small commercial customers throughout Dane County and southern Wisconsin. Its offerings include roof-mounted residential systems, ground-mount arrays for sites where roof installation is not feasible, and custom commercial installations for local businesses. The team manages each project from initial consultation and site assessment through system design, permitting, installation, activation, and ongoing support.

Midwest Solar Power serves homeowners seeking to reduce energy bills and businesses looking to lower operating costs through renewable energy. Commercial clients include small businesses in the Madison area that want tailored solar solutions designed to maximize investment and environmental impact. The company also assists customers with navigating incentives such as the federal 30% investment tax credit and emerging programs like the Home Energy Assistance Rebate (HEAR) program.

The firm distinguishes itself by emphasizing honest, high-quality work at a fair price and by treating each installation as unique, requiring a deep understanding of how the solar array interacts with the existing structure. This approach, combined with a full-service process from consultation to post-installation support, is intended to deliver a hassle-free transition to sustainable energy for every client.

name: Midwest Solars
old_description: Midwest Solars started in 2019 as a dream between friends Tom Wingert, owner of Tecom LLC and Andy Van Roo.
about:
Midwest Solars is based in Mondovi, Wisconsin, and was founded in 2019 by Tom Wingert, owner of the 15-year-old Florida corporation Tecom LLC, and Andy Van Roo. The two friends launched the venture as a division of Tecom LLC, with their first project being a commercial building owned by Van Roo in rural western Wisconsin.

The company provides residential and commercial solar panel installation, energy storage system integration, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. It has installed dozens of energy storage devices over the past nine years and is actively developing multi-megawatt projects in Wisconsin, Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Vermont, while serving customers across all 50 states.

Midwest Solars serves homeowners, businesses, and industrial clients seeking solar generation and storage solutions. Its project portfolio spans commercial rooftops, industrial facilities, and data-center hybrid energy systems that combine solar with natural gas turbines. The company also works with clients navigating governmental incentives such as the Inflation Reduction Act.

Founder Tom Wingert’s decade of experience at Tesla Energy and Amazon Global Flight Logistics gives the firm deep expertise in energy storage, which it says places it years ahead of competitors. The company emphasizes a no-nonsense approach to delivering affordable, working solutions and aims to make energy essentially available at a cost closer to free.
